Philip Glass, born in 1937, is a prolific American composer and pianist who is one of the most influential and widely celebrated figures in late-twentieth-century classical music. He is a primary pioneer of minimalism, though he dislikes the term and prefers to describe his style as music with repetitive structures, building large-scale compositions out of small, repeating melodic cells and additive rhythms. Glass has achieved immense mainstream success across multiple genres, composing symphonies, concertos, film scores, and landmark avant-garde operas.

Einstein on the Beach from 1976 is his first and most famous opera, a five-hour plotless collaboration with director Robert Wilson. Its libretto consists entirely of numbers, solfège syllables, and poetry read over a repeating solo violin played by a performer dressed as Albert Einstein. The Portrait Trilogy is the collective name for his three early biographical operas about figures who transformed the world through ideas: Einstein on the Beach exploring science, Satyagraha from 1980 depicting Mahatma Gandhi in South Africa with a Sanskrit text, and Akhnaten from 1983 centering on the monotheistic Egyptian pharaoh. Koyaanisqatsi from 1982 is his iconic score for Godfrey Reggio's non-narrative cult film, featuring a deep bass vocal repeating the Hopi title word, meaning life out of balance, alongside rapidly undulating organ and brass arpeggios. Glassworks from 1982 is a six-movement studio album designed to introduce Glass's music to a wider pop audience, featuring accessible, melodic movements like the opening Opening for solo piano.

Ravi Shankar, the legendary Indian sitar player, was a crucial influence on Glass. Glass assisted Shankar in Paris in the nineteen sixties, and transcribing Shankar's music introduced Glass to the non-Western additive rhythmic cycles that replaced traditional Western bar lines in his music. The Philip Glass Ensemble is the performing group he founded in 1968, comprising woodwinds, keyboards, and amplified vocals, which toured extensively to perform his early experimental compositions. Glass is a leader of the American minimalist movement along with Steve Reich, Terry Riley, and La Monte Young, having re-envisioned the operatic form by replacing narrative plots with thematic, ritualistic tableaus.
